title: Canonical EFT and strong-coupling audit for a suppressed zero-mode kinetic norm
assumptions: one physical time and the positive-signature scalar zero-mode benchmark of versions 0.6 and 0.7
brane current coupling scale F0=M_b^2 sqrt(V_W) before canonical normalization
leading shift-symmetric self interaction c_X (partial q)^4/Lambda_0^4
radiation domination at electroweak sphaleron freeze-out
current-loop estimate is naive dimensional analysis rather than a computed 6D loop result

interpretation.secured_result: canonical normalization enhances every operator according to its number of q fields; the desired current enhancement cannot be assessed in isolation
interpretation.generic_kk_result: an order-one X^2 operator suppressed by M_KK becomes strongly coupled many orders of magnitude below the electroweak audit scale for Z_eff near 1e-16
interpretation.uv_only_result: if the leading X^2 operator is genuinely suppressed by M6 and no comparable KK-scale operator is generated, a narrow conditional Z_eff window can exist for safety factor one
interpretation.sequestering_burden: the coefficient of any M_KK-suppressed X^2 operator must be extraordinarily small and requires an explicit symmetry or matching calculation
interpretation.potential_result: an unprotected quartic or mass is amplified by inverse powers of Z_eff; a shift symmetry or equivalent protection is required
interpretation.not_a_global_no_go: the audit blocks the generic unprotected KK-EFT realization, not every topological, axionic or symmetry-protected higher-dimensional source

limitations: only one representative X^2 self operator is included
the full tower of higher derivative operators and mixed metric-flux-radion interactions is not matched
the coefficient c_X at M_KK is not computed from KK exchange
NDA current-loop estimates do not replace a regulator- and basis-consistent 6D loop calculation
exact shift symmetry, anomaly structure and its breaking are not derived from the parent action
no evidence effect; K1-D and K1-E remain closed
